_disclaimer: Illustrative source registry for the chinese-herbal-oncology-support PROPOSAL only. verification_status=verified means this pass independently re-checked the claim via live search/fetch on the date below; pending_manual_verification means first-pass triage from the supplied description, not independently re-confirmed. Nothing here is a clinical or legal determination; inclusion is not endorsement.

_search_metadata.note: No claim of a comprehensive Chinese-language search is made. ChiCTR, SinoMed, CNKI, and Wanfang were NOT searched in this pass -- access and a qualified bilingual clinical reviewer were not available. Any Chinese-language primary literature referenced here comes only from what English-language secondary sources (reviews, PDQ, Cochrane) themselves cite, which is a material limitation recorded in source-assessment.md and interview-decisions.md (H2-007).

sources.title: 2019 narrative/mechanistic review of TCM compounds in cancer (curcumin, resveratrol, berberine, and others)
sources.publisher: PMC-indexed journal (publisher not re-verified in this pass)
sources.notes: Per the proposal brief, much of the discussion is cell/animal/molecular/mechanistic research on compounds that are not unique to TCM and not equivalent to whole formulas. Used as a discovery map only; every clinical-sounding claim must be traced to its own exact human study before any card cites it directly.

sources.title: Cancer Council NSW -- Chinese herbal medicine
sources.notes: Reviewed patient education; useful safety/context baseline. Its American-ginseng-for-fatigue reference must be checked against the exact species/trial/current guideline (see src-asco-sio-2024-fatigue, src-barton-2013-ginseng) and never generalized to Asian ginseng or other formulas.

sources.title: HealthTree -- Traditional Chinese Medicine in Cancer
sources.notes: Patient-education/advocacy content, not primary evidence. Publication date, authorship, review process, and cited sources not independently re-confirmed in this pass; access_status recorded honestly as unverified rather than inferring content.

sources.title: Cancer Research UK -- Essiac
sources.notes: VERIFIED via live search: 'There is no scientific evidence to use it as a treatment for cancer... NCI tested Essiac several times... found Essiac had no anti-cancer effects.' Also notes MSK laboratory testing found no anticancer features.

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters -- Essiac
sources.notes: Tertiary background only -- used to help identify names/claimed composition/references that must then be independently verified, never as efficacy evidence.

sources.title: BioRes Scientia -- Traditional herbal medicine in supportive cancer care: from alternative to integrative (2025 narrative review, multi-tradition)
sources.publisher: BioRes Scientia (journal/publisher not independently verified for indexing/peer-review rigor in this pass)
sources.notes: Broad narrative review spanning multiple traditions; journal indexing, peer-review claims, methods, citations, conflicts, and correction status not independently re-verified. Broad benefit statements are discovery leads only.

sources.title: The Application of Traditional Chinese Medicine-Derived Formulations in Cancer Immunotherapy: A Review (received 2024-10-26, accepted 2024-12-21, published 2025-01)
sources.notes: VERIFIED via live fetch. Covers breast (HER2+/triple-negative), papillary thyroid, osteosarcoma, colorectal, and hepatocellular cancer; cited findings are predominantly cell/animal/mechanistic (SK-BR-3, TPC-1, MG-63 cell lines; PI3K/AKT, NF-kB, Wnt/beta-catenin pathways), with limited human RCT evidence. Contains this exact unsafe, unsupported statement: 'Western medicine usually eliminates tumors through sectioning and surgery, which inevitably leads to the consequences of tumor spread.' This statement is NOT reproduced anywhere in this proposal's cards and must never be repeated as fact -- surgical resection is standard, evidence-based curative-intent treatment for many solid tumors, and no card in this proposal may imply otherwise.

sources.title: Wikipedia -- List of forms of alternative medicine
sources.license_metadata: Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0 per site-wide terms; this registry stores only a modality-name index, not reproduced article text.
sources.revision_note: Snapshot taken 2026-09-17; a collaboratively edited page has no fixed revision id recorded in this pass -- recorded as a discovery/taxonomy aid only, never as clinical evidence, consistent with its evidence_eligibility.
sources.notes: Used exclusively to build knowledge/chinese-herbal-oncology/alternative_modality_screening.json's discovery inventory. Cannot substantiate safety, efficacy, mechanism, cultural origin, or nutrition advice for any entry.

sources.title: Memorial Healthcare System -- Cancer Fighting Herbs and Spices (2016)
sources.notes: VERIFIED via live search. Despite health-system provenance and (per the brief) a dietitian byline, this is a provider blog, not a reproducible evidence review. Confirmed claims/advice this proposal explicitly does NOT reuse: mixing turmeric with black pepper/olive oil to 'activate and help with absorption' (piperine-enhancement advice); describing garlic as 'the most powerful anti-cancer spice' that 'helps boost the immune system'; a one-clove-per-day garlic dose with a 10-minute-rest-for-allicin-formation instruction; ginger tea framed as protecting against cancer via antioxidant/anti-inflammatory action. Registered discovery_only / provider_education; rejected as sole support for efficacy, prevention, dosing, or interaction-management claims.

sources.title: 2016 descriptive cross-sectional survey (n=150) of self-reported herbal-remedy/functional-food use among breast, prostate, and colorectal cancer patients at two Trinidad specialty clinics; data collected 2012
sources.notes: Documents use/beliefs (soursop, wheatgrass, saffron, aloe, garlic, ginger, beetroot, carrot, papaya, mixed juices) -- did NOT objectively test tumor response, symptom benefit, safety, survival, or comparative efficacy. Convenience sample from two clinics, 2012 data. Used only for prevalence/disclosure/interaction-safety-design questions, never to infer a cancer-type recommendation or that any reported item is beneficial.

sources.title: NCCIH -- Turmeric

sources.title: NCCIH -- Ginger
sources.notes: Re-check live before any citation; brief notes evidence for ginger added to standard chemo-nausea treatment is uncertain.

sources.title: NCCIH -- Garlic
sources.notes: Re-check live before any citation; brief notes garlic does not appear to lower stomach-cancer risk, colorectal-prevention evidence is uncertain, and garlic supplements can increase bleeding risk.

sources.notes: Primary source for the green-tea/EGCG-bortezomib interaction record and general food/supplement-drug interaction framing.

sources.title: NCI PDQ -- Medicinal Mushrooms (health-professional)
sources.notes: Primary source for Ganoderma/reishi and PSK/Trametes versicolor framing alongside the Cochrane review.

sources.title: NCI PDQ -- Essiac/Flor Essence (patient and health-professional)
sources.notes: VERIFIED via live search: 'No controlled data are available from human studies to suggest that Essiac or Flor Essence are effective in the treatment of patients with cancer.' Also: some evidence suggests Flor Essence may INCREASE tumor formation in an animal model of breast cancer -- a safety signal, not merely an absence-of-benefit finding.

sources.title: Chung et al. 2015 -- overview of systematic reviews of Chinese herbal medicine (PMID 26669761)
sources.note_on_search_currency: Per the proposal brief, this overview searched only through 2014 -- now roughly 12 years out of date at the time of this pass.
sources.notes: Primary source for card-mixed-advanced-cancers-heterogeneous-formulas; reported possible quality-of-life signals but flagged contributory-review-methodology and conflicting survival/toxicity evidence.

sources.title: McCulloch et al. 2006 -- Astragalus-based Chinese herbs and platinum-based chemotherapy for advanced NSCLC: meta-analysis of randomized trials (JCO 2006;24(3):419-430)
sources.notes: VERIFIED via live search: 34 RCTs, 2815 patients on cisplatin-based chemotherapy for advanced NSCLC; reduced risk of death at 12 months (RR 0.67) and improved tumor response (RR 1.34) with added Astragalus-based herbs, but the source itself states several included studies were of poor quality and findings need confirmation in well-designed trials -- reappraisal explicitly required, not a standalone tumor-control recommendation.

sources.title: Li et al. 2013 -- systematic review of Chinese herbal medicine as adjunctive therapy for advanced NSCLC
sources.notes: Registered per brief; full re-verification of methods/results pending.

sources.title: Cochrane CD007731 -- Ganoderma lucidum (Reishi mushroom) for cancer treatment (Jin et al.; pub2 2012, pub3 2016 update, PMID 27045603)
sources.notes: VERIFIED via live search. Latest update (pub3, 2016): 5 RCTs, 373 subjects total, studies predominantly small, Chinese-population-only, methodological quality concerns; supportive signal alongside chemo/radiotherapy, not evidence for first-line cancer treatment. The proposal brief's supplied URL pointed to pub2 (2012); pub3 (2016) is the current version and is the one cited here.

sources.title: ASCO-SIO 2024 guideline update -- Management of Fatigue in Adult Survivors of Cancer (PMID 38754041; JCO.24.00541)
sources.notes: VERIFIED via live search: American ginseng is a conditional recommendation, low-quality evidence, specifically for adults ON ACTIVE TREATMENT (distinguished from tai chi/qigong also during treatment, versus yoga/acupressure/moxibustion for after treatment completion). Evidence base: 113 RCTs across all fatigue interventions; certainty low-to-moderate overall.

sources.title: Barton et al. -- randomized trial of American ginseng (Panax quinquefolius) for cancer-related fatigue (PMID 23853057)
sources.publisher: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
sources.notes: Primary RCT underlying part of the ASCO-SIO American-ginseng recommendation; exact species (Panax quinquefolius, NOT Panax ginseng) must never be conflated with Asian ginseng.

sources.title: ESPEN practical guideline on clinical nutrition in cancer
sources.notes: Primary baseline source for the diet templates, reused from the sibling Ayurveda proposal's citation where applicable.

sources.title: ASCO guideline on exercise, diet, and weight management during cancer treatment
sources.notes: Primary source for survivorship-nutrition template gating (only applied when nutritionally stable and guideline-supported).

sources.title: Memorial Sloan Kettering -- Graviola (soursop) monograph
sources.notes: VERIFIED via live search: human anticancer evidence lacking; concentrated leaf/seed/bark extracts contain higher annonacin (an acetogenin) concentrations linked to atypical Parkinsonism with very high long-term consumption -- a real neurologic safety signal, not merely 'insufficient evidence of benefit.'
